method_card.title: Family Members and Descriptions
method_card.content:
This lesson covers family vocabulary, possessive adjectives and physical/personality descriptions.

FrenchEnglish
le pèrefather
la mèremother
le frèrebrother
la sœursister
le grand-pèregrandfather
la grand-mèregrandmother
l'oncleuncle
la tanteaunt
le cousin / la cousinecousin
le filsson
la filledaughter
le beau-pèrestepfather
la belle-mèrestepmother

Possessive adjectives agree with the noun they describe, not the owner: mon (m), ma (f), mes (pl) = my; son (m), sa (f), ses (pl) = his/her. Exception: before a feminine noun starting with a vowel, use mon/ton/son instead of ma/ta/sa.

Physical descriptions: Use avoir for hair and eyes (J'ai les cheveux blonds), être for build and personality (Elle est grande et sympa). Adjectives must agree in gender and number.

Model: Mon père s'appelle Marc. Il a les cheveux courts et bruns. Il est grand et sympa. Ma mère est petite et très gentille.
steps: Learn the key family members in masculine/feminine pairs
Master possessive adjectives (mon/ma/mes, ton/ta/tes, son/sa/ses)
Practice describing physical appearance using avoir and être
Write full sentences combining family, possessives and descriptions

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Mon frère a les cheveux noirs et il est assez grand.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Break the sentence into chunks: Mon frère | a les cheveux noirs | et | il est assez grand.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Mon frère = My brother. a les cheveux noirs = has black hair (avoir for physical features).

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: il est assez grand = he is quite tall (être for build).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: My brother has black hair and he is quite tall.

worked_examples.question: How do you choose between mon, ma and mes?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Look at the noun you are describing — is it masculine, feminine or plural?

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Masculine singular → mon (mon père). Feminine singular → ma (ma mère). Plural → mes (mes parents).

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Exception: feminine noun starting with a vowel → use mon for pronunciation. Example: mon amie (not ma amie).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: The possessive adjective agrees with the gender/number of the thing owned, not the owner. Mon (m), ma (f), mes (pl), with the vowel exception.

method_card.title: Friendships and Qualities
method_card.content:
This lesson covers friendship vocabulary, opinion phrases, and the near future tense (le futur proche).

FrenchEnglish
un(e) ami(e)a friend
un copain / une copinea mate/friend
le/la meilleur(e) ami(e)best friend
s'entendre bien avecto get on well with
se disputer avecto argue with
passer du temps avecto spend time with
la confiancetrust
le soutiensupport
fidèleloyal
honnêtehonest
drôlefunny
Je pense queI think that

Near future tense: aller (conjugated) + infinitive. Je vais sortir = I am going to go out. Nous allons jouer = We are going to play. This is the easiest way to add a future time frame to your writing.

Model: Mon meilleur ami s'appelle Thomas. Je m'entends très bien avec lui car il est fidèle et honnête. Ce week-end, nous allons jouer au foot ensemble.
steps: Learn the key friendship vocabulary and qualities
Master opinion phrases (à mon avis, je pense que, je trouve que)
Form the near future tense with aller + infinitive
Practice combining opinions with reasons using car and parce que

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Je m'entends bien avec ma copine car elle est drôle.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Break it down: Je m'entends bien avec | ma copine | car | elle est drôle.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Je m'entends bien avec = I get on well with. ma copine = my (female) friend.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: car = because. elle est drôle = she is funny.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I get on well with my friend because she is funny.

worked_examples.question: How do you form the near future tense?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Take the present tense of aller: je vais, tu vas, il/elle va, nous allons, vous allez, ils/elles vont.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Add the infinitive of the main verb directly after: je vais jouer = I am going to play.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Example: Nous allons aller au cinéma ensemble = We are going to go to the cinema together.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Conjugated aller + infinitive. E.g. je vais sortir, elle va rencontrer, nous allons jouer.

method_card.title: Relationships, Marriage and Future Plans
method_card.content:
This lesson covers relationships and marriage vocabulary, pros and cons of marriage, and the conditional tense.

FrenchEnglish
le couplecouple
le/la partenairepartner
le mariagemarriage/wedding
se marierto get married
le PACScivil partnership
se séparerto separate
célibatairesingle
l'amourlove
sortir avecto go out with
tomber amoureux/amoureuseto fall in love
je voudraisI would like
j'aimeraisI would like

The conditional tense: infinitive + imperfect endings (-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient). Irregular stems: être → ser-, avoir → aur-, aller → ir-, faire → fer-, vouloir → voudr-, pouvoir → pourr-.

Model: À l'avenir, je voudrais me marier et avoir deux enfants. J'aimerais que mon partenaire soit gentil et honnête. Ce serait idéal d'habiter à la campagne.
steps: Learn the key relationship and marriage vocabulary
Practice giving pros and cons of marriage
Form the conditional tense with infinitive + imperfect endings
Use conditional structures for future plans (je voudrais, j'aimerais, ce serait)

exam_context.frequency: Common topic in 90-word and 150-word writing tasks

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Le mariage coûte très cher.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Break it down: Le mariage | coûte | très cher.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Le mariage = Marriage. coûte = costs. très cher = very expensive.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Marriage costs a lot of money. / Marriage is very expensive.

worked_examples.question: How do you form 'I would like' in French?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Take the infinitive aimer and add the imperfect ending for je: -ais.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: aimer + -ais = j'aimerais. You can also use vouloir with its irregular stem: voudr- + -ais = je voudrais.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: j'aimerais or je voudrais — both mean 'I would like' and use the conditional tense.

wrong.veux: veux is present tense (I want). The sentence needs the conditional: voudrais (I would like).
wrong.vais: vais is near future (I am going to). The sentence uses would like, so use the conditional.

gaps.correct_explain: avoir is the infinitive — after je voudrais, use the infinitive form.

wrong.ai: ai is conjugated present tense. After voudrais, use the infinitive avoir.

method_card.title: Healthy Living and Lifestyle
method_card.content:
This lesson covers health and fitness vocabulary, il faut + infinitive for giving advice, and reflexive verbs for daily routines.

FrenchEnglish
la santéhealth
en bonne santéin good health
en formefit / in shape
sain(e)healthy
équilibré(e)balanced
il fautit is necessary to / you must
il ne faut pasyou must not
fumerto smoke
le tabactobacco
se coucherto go to bed
se leverto get up
se détendreto relax

il faut + infinitive = you must / it is necessary to. Il faut bien manger = You must eat well. Il ne faut pas fumer = You must not smoke.

Reflexive verbs: subject + reflexive pronoun (me/te/se/nous/vous/se) + verb. Je me couche à dix heures = I go to bed at 10. Il se lève tôt = He gets up early.

Model: Pour être en bonne santé, il faut bien manger et bien dormir. Je me lève à sept heures et je me couche à dix heures. Il ne faut pas fumer.

Master il faut + infinitive for giving advice
Practice conjugating reflexive verbs for daily routines
Combine health advice with opinions and reasons

method_card.title: Food, Drink and Mealtimes
method_card.content:
This lesson covers food and drink vocabulary, partitive articles (du, de la, de l', des), and describing mealtimes.

FrenchEnglish
le painbread
le fromagecheese
le poissonfish
le pouletchicken
la viandemeat
les fruitsfruit
les légumesvegetables
le gâteaucake
la glaceice cream
l'eau (f)water
le jus d'orangeorange juice
le petit déjeunerbreakfast
le déjeunerlunch
le dînerdinner

Partitive articles: du (masculine) = du pain; de la (feminine) = de la viande; de l' (vowel) = de l'eau; des (plural) = des fruits. After a negative → de/d': Je ne mange pas de viande.

Model: Au petit déjeuner, je mange du pain et du fromage. Je bois du jus d'orange. Au dîner, je mange de la viande et des légumes. Je ne mange pas de glace.
steps: Learn the key food and drink vocabulary
Master partitive articles (du, de la, de l', des)
Know that partitives become de/d' after a negative
Practice describing meals at breakfast, lunch and dinner

worked_examples.question: How do partitive articles change after a negative?

steps.content: In positive sentences: du, de la, de l', des.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: After ne...pas, ALL partitives become de (or d' before a vowel).

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Example: Je mange du poisson → Je ne mange pas de poisson.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: After a negative, du/de la/de l'/des all become de (or d' before a vowel).

method_card.title: Sport and Staying Active
method_card.content:
This lesson covers sport vocabulary, jouer à vs faire de, and the passé composé with être (DR MRS P VANDERTRAMP).

FrenchEnglish
le footballfootball
le tennistennis
le basketbasketball
la natationswimming
le cyclismecycling
la gymnastiquegymnastics
l'athlétismeathletics
l'équitationhorse riding
la musculationweight training
garder la formeto keep fit
passionnant(e)exciting

jouer à = to play (team/ball sports): jouer au foot (m), jouer à la pétanque (f), jouer aux cartes (pl).

faire de = to do (individual sports/activities): faire du vélo (m), faire de la natation (f), faire de l'équitation (vowel).

Passé composé with être: DR MRS P VANDERTRAMP verbs + reflexive verbs use être. Past participle agrees: Elle est allée (f), Ils sont allés (m.pl).
steps: Learn sports vocabulary with correct genders
Use jouer à for team/ball sports and faire de for individual activities
Know the DR MRS P VANDERTRAMP verbs that use être in the passé composé
Practice past participle agreement with être

exam_context.frequency: Common in speaking and writing tasks

steps.label: Step 2

steps.label: Answer

steps.label: Step 2

steps.label: Answer

method_card.content:
This lesson covers school subject vocabulary, giving opinions with reasons, telling the time, and describing your timetable.

Opinions: Ma matière préférée, c'est... + parce que / car + reason. Je suis fort(e) en... = I am good at. Je suis nul(le) en... = I am rubbish at.

Telling the time: Il est huit heures (8:00), et quart (quarter past), et demie (half past), moins le quart (quarter to).
steps: Learn the school subjects in French with their genders

method_card.title: Jobs, Work Experience and Future Plans
method_card.content:
This lesson covers job titles, work experience vocabulary, and future plans using three tenses.

FrenchEnglish
un médecindoctor
un(e) infirmier/infirmièrenurse
un(e) professeur(e)teacher
un(e) avocat(e)lawyer
un(e) ingénieur(e)engineer
un(e) coiffeur/coiffeusehairdresser
un stagework placement
une entreprisecompany
le salairesalary
je voudrais devenirI would like to become
à l'avenirin the future

Job title gender: -eur → -euse (coiffeur/coiffeuse), -ier → -ière (infirmier/infirmière), -teur → -trice (acteur/actrice).

Three future structures: Near future: je vais étudier. Conditional: je voudrais devenir. Simple future: je travaillerai. Using all three shows excellent range.

Model: J'ai fait un stage dans un magasin. C'était une bonne expérience. À l'avenir, je voudrais devenir médecin. Je vais étudier à l'université.
steps: Learn job titles in both masculine and feminine forms
